_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph
params.convention: The sampling period of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard, 20 Hz (one scene every 50 ms): the step bound of headingSince, the largest gap between two consecutive scenes it integrates across; not a look-back window and not an action window.

params.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
params.source: Naturalistic-driving and simulator stop-detection practice (SHRP 2 event coding; CARLA ground-truth velocity resolution).

params.name: p.crosswalk_reach
params.convention: Reach within which a road user counts as at a crossing: a vehicle halted for a crosswalk stands within the stop-line set-back before it plus a positioning margin; a pedestrian waiting at the kerb stands within the same reach.
params.source: MUTCD (2009) Section 3B.16, stop and yield line placement before a crosswalk.

params.name: p.same_direction_tolerance
params.convention: Cosine of the largest angle between two headings counted as the same direction of travel (thirty degrees), covering lane curvature and lane changes.
params.source: Trajectory-processing conventions for same-direction classification (NGSIM, highD).

params.name: p.conflict_horizon
params.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a projected approach of the centres within this time counts toward the danger of a crash.
params.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Hyden (1987) Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique; van der Horst (1990) TTC thresholds.

params.name: p.conflict_clearance
params.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the bodies of two passenger vehicles would touch or nearly touch (about a half-length plus a half-width of a design passenger car).
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, design vehicle P dimensions.

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: Window within which a turn at a junction or across a median, including a U-turn made in several movements, is completed.
params.source: Turning-movement durations in naturalistic intersection data (single turns of a few seconds; multi-point U-turns longer).

params.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
params.convention: Lower bound of a turn: a leftward heading change below it is a drift or lane change, not a turn onto another way.
params.source: Turning-movement classification in trajectory datasets (inD, NGSIM intersection data).

params.name: p.left_turn_max_angle
params.convention: Upper bound of a left turn, above which the direction of travel counts as reversed (a U-turn).
params.source: Turning-movement classification in trajectory datasets (inD, NGSIM intersection data).

params.name: p.u_turn_min_angle
params.convention: Heading change at or beyond which the direction of travel counts as reversed.
params.source: Turning-movement classification in trajectory datasets (inD, NGSIM intersection data).

params.name: p.u_turn_max_angle
params.convention: Heading change beyond which the road user has turned past the opposite direction (a loop rather than a reversal).
params.source: Turning-movement classification in trajectory datasets (inD, NGSIM intersection data).

params.name: p.turn_yaw_tolerance
params.convention: Yaw rate below which a change of heading counts as none: above lane-keeping yaw noise, below the yaw rates of turning at a junction.
params.source: Vehicle-dynamics practice for turn-onset detection from yaw-rate sensors.

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the ontology's approach convention: the body-to-mark distance within which a halt counts as made at the mark, and beyond which the road user is outside the stopping zone.
params.source: MUTCD (2009) Section 3B.16 stop line placement; positioning accuracy of stop-compliance studies.

params.name: p.opposite_direction_tolerance
params.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which two approach directions still count as opposite (thirty degrees), covering skewed approaches.
params.source: Trajectory-processing conventions for opposing-movement classification at intersections (inD).

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_time
params.convention: Critical headway of gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle whose time to reach the intersection is below it is too close for a turning or crossing manoeuvre to be completed ahead of it.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual, 6th ed., base critical headway for a major-street left turn.

params.name: p.decel_tolerance
params.convention: Longitudinal deceleration below which a sampled acceleration counts as none: above coasting and sensor noise, below deliberate braking.
params.source: Naturalistic-driving braking-event detection practice (SHRP 2; 100-Car study).

params.name: p.yield_slowing_distance
params.convention: Distance travelled before the stopping zone within which a slowing for a yield sign counts as made for that sign: the braking distance of an urban approach.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance at urban approach speeds.

params.name: p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance
params.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the body of a passenger vehicle and a pedestrian would touch or nearly touch: about a design passenger car's half-length plus a pedestrian's body radius.
params.source: design passenger car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P) and pedestrian body ellipse (HCM)

params.name: p.right_turn_min_angle
params.convention: Lower bound of a right turn: a rightward heading change below it is a drift or lane change, not a turn onto another way.
params.source: junction turning geometry, mirrored from the left-turn band

params.name: p.right_turn_max_angle
params.convention: Upper bound of a right turn, above which the direction of travel counts as reversed.
params.source: junction turning geometry, mirrored from the left-turn band

params.name: p.perception_reaction_time
params.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from the appearance of a hazard to the application of the brakes.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

params.name: p.stopping_decel_dry
params.convention: Deceleration a driver attains in a controlled stop on a dry paved surface.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book and braking studies (Fambro et al., NCHRP 400)

params.name: p.stopping_decel_wet
params.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers attain on a wet pavement.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

params.name: p.stopping_decel_ice
params.convention: Deceleration attainable on an icy or snow-covered surface, from the low friction coefficient of such surfaces.
params.source: winter road friction measurements (PIARC)

params.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
params.convention: Side-friction limit of horizontal curve design: the lateral acceleration a curve may impose on a vehicle at a comfortable, safe speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, horizontal curve side friction factors

params.name: p.lane_width_speed_time
params.convention: Lane width per unit of speed from the lane-width and design-speed relation of highway design guides (a full-width lane for a high design speed): the speed times it may not exceed the lane's width.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book lane widths by design speed
